sections.label: The opening
sections.line: Provider terms, not technology, stalled VoiceDebrief's business model
sections.para: VoiceDebrief transcribes, translates and debriefs a voice note in the browser on the user's own key, about a third of a penny for 42 seconds. Its commercial model, a capped key handed to a paying user, is what OpenRouter's terms forbid. ElevenLabs is the nearest fit, and the article ends with a brief for asking providers.

sections.label: In short
sections.line: The product works; provider terms blocked its business model
sections.para: No server is the product: the audio is never seen. The plan was a five-pound payment, a cut, and the rest as a credit limit on a key, which OpenRouter's docs describe and section 7(4) forbids. Most providers cannot cap a key; ElevenLabs can, with OEM terms and Scribe at $0.22 an hour.

sections.label: What VoiceDebrief is
sections.line: Built fast in the open, then commits abruptly stopped
sections.para: Drop any audio file and get a transcript, translation and debrief, with costs quoted before the pass and nothing kept. The first commit was on 28 July 2026, with 48, 127 and 64 commits in the first three weeks, then none, then eleven, then three. The last commit was on 7 September.

sections.label: Why no server is the product
sections.line: No server is the product, not a preference
sections.para: With no server the audio is never seen, which removes data custody, breach risk, shared keys, billing, user databases, scaling and on-call. A static page costs the same for one user or a million. Adding a server brings all of it back at once, which is a different company.

sections.label: The commercial model that was never a billing system
sections.line: The plan was billing by not building billing
sections.para: A user pays through Stripe, a key is created with their share as its credit limit, and the provider meters it; a five-pound minimum covers card fees. OpenRouter's Management API supports exactly this, but its terms of 31 August 2026 forbid reselling access and transferring credits. An enterprise agreement might open the door.

sections.label: The map: every provider, from their own pages
sections.line: Only OpenRouter and ElevenLabs can cap a key
sections.para: Read on 12 October 2026: Groq, Mistral and OpenAI cap the organisation or workspace, Deepgram keys expire but do not meter, and cloud budgets act after the fact. ElevenLabs has per-key credit quotas and OEM terms letting a business set its own end-user price. The providers that can cap keys say most about resale.

sections.label: The four routes
sections.line: Four routes remain, and only one needs no permission
sections.para: Route one, capped OpenRouter keys, is forbidden by standard terms, and route two asks ElevenLabs to allow a capped key under OEM terms. Route three, bring your own key, runs today but is a wall. Route four, a metering proxy, needs nobody's permission but brings back the backend.

sections.label: The brief for the agents that will write to them
sections.line: One sentence to ask every provider: sell capped keys
sections.para: Messages from the agents, sent by Dinis, state no server, the model as a property of the key, user-owned ceilings and full openness. The ask is to let a credit limit be a property of a key a user buys. Each provider gets a tailored request, and every answer is recorded as a repository issue.

sections.label: What this does not claim
sections.line: Terms are quoted, not interpreted; route two may fail
sections.para: Every clause is quoted from pages read on 12 October 2026 and is not legal advice. When OpenRouter's clause arrived is unknown, and AssemblyAI, Groq and Mistral terms were not read. Commit counts show when work stopped, not why, and ElevenLabs may say no.

sections.label: Where this comes from
sections.line: Sources: the product, its repository and provider pages
sections.para: VoiceDebrief's site, key page and public repository, read on 12 October 2026, and its 28 July brief pack. Provider pages include OpenRouter's terms and Management API, ElevenLabs' terms, OEM terms and Grants, Deepgram, Groq, Mistral, OpenAI, AssemblyAI, AWS Budgets, Portkey and Puter.
